issues: False boundary-test claim in the 'single-gene-wrong-values' probe annotation: the rationale states b0979's growth is shifted by '+5e-9, deliberately inside the published 1e-8 absolute tolerance floor, testing the boundary', and the probe concerns repeat 'we test a clearly legal perturbation (5e-9 absolute on a 0.87 phenotype, inside the floor)'. The actual script writes 0.8739220069684307 against reference 0.8739215069684307, a difference of 5.0e-7 — 50x outside the 1.087e-8 limit — and the recorded grader message confirms "|diff|=5.000e-07 > 1.087e-08". No within-floor perturbation was executed by this probe. As recorded, the evidence falsely suggests the grader rejected an in-tolerance value, i.e. that the published tolerance is not honored. A value actually inside the tolerance (e.g. a genuine +5e-9 giving 0.8739215119684307) would pass per the grader code. Action: correct the probe rationale and concern text so the record accurately states the b0979 edit is a 5e-7 out-of-tolerance mutation (arithmetic slip: 5e-7 written where 5e-9 was intended), and note that within-tolerance acceptance is established separately by the valid-representation control (1e-12 perturbations passing all checks) and by the recomputed/alternative controls (cross-run noise ~5e-13 passing). Keep the frozen mutation script, name and focus unchanged; only the annotation is corrected, then re-run all controls on the revised candidate.

Minor public-contract/implementation divergence on infeasible growth tokens: the public rules state the accepted representations are 'an empty cell or the literal text NaN' (the checks text also says 'the token NaN'), but the grader's parse_growth accepts any case-insensitive signed variant ('nan', '-nan', '+nan'). This can let a submission using e.g. 'NAN' pass the executable checks while violating the published rule as written. Action: either restrict the grader to the literal 'NaN' token and empty cells as published, or amend the public rule to state the accepted NaN tokens exactly as implemented; pick one and make rule and code agree.

Advisory (no action blocking, do not change science or tolerance): the task brief states near-zero objective values 'must be written as-is and must not be clamped to zero', while the acceptance rules admit an exact 0.0 within the 1e-8 floor for a reference near-zero noise value. The addendum explicitly discloses this and it is the only sound treatment, since the reference's own repeat runs (repeatability records: non-identical row multisets across replays) and both independently executed correct implementations produce 0.0 or differing ~1e-16 values at those targets. Retain the disclosed addendum reconciliation; optionally clarify in the public text that the as-is requirement for near-zero magnitudes is enforced only up to the published tolerance.
rationale: The candidate is scientifically sound on coverage and comparison design: all three terminal source endpoints (137 single-gene, 95 single-reaction, 4560 diagonal-inclusive double-reaction targets) are exported and requested; the diagonal-included 4560-row interpretation is empirically confirmed by the reference passing double_target_set_complete; the 1e-8 + 1e-9|ref| tolerance is defensible (measured cross-run noise ~5e-13, >4 orders below the floor; smallest meaningful phenotype ~0.077, >6 orders above it; the floor legitimately admits raw 0.0 vs ~1e-16 noise, disclosed in the addendum); meaningful wrong results (1e-5 shifts, distinct phenotype substitutions, fabricated infeasible growth, status flips, pair-key corruption, diagonal drift) all fail without relying on crashes; misplaced outputs/ nesting and missing/empty files fail correctly per the actual submission hash records; all 14 executed controls match the control_summary. However, one annotation in the evidence record is materially false: the single-gene-wrong-values probe claims a +5e-9 within-tolerance boundary perturbation on b0979, but the script and recorded grader output show a 5.0e-7 difference (|diff|=5.000e-07 > 1.087e-08) that fails. The out-of-tolerance failure coverage for that file remains real (b2288 ~0.16 away, b1723 ~0.87 away), and within-tolerance acceptance is separately established by the valid-representation control, so the mutation itself and its recorded outcome are valid — but the record as written falsely implies the grader rejected an in-tolerance value, i.e. that the published tolerance is not honored. That claim must be corrected (annotation only; the frozen script, name and focus stay unchanged) before packaging. Two lesser items (grader accepting case-insensitive/signed NaN variants broader than the published 'empty or literal NaN' rule, and the disclosed task-brief/addendum tension on near-zero clamping) should also be addressed or aligned.

source_coverage.rationale: The three terminal scientific results of the executed source are the named, stored variables deletion_results (all single gene deletions, 137 rows), single (all single reaction deletions, 95 rows) and double (full reaction double-deletion table, 4560 rows); the exported reference CSVs have exactly those row counts and schemas (ids,growth,status), confirming no eligible terminal endpoint was dropped. Exclusions are source-backed and legitimate: subset deletion demonstrations (genes[:20], reactions[:20], double_gene_deletion on genes[-5:] with .round(4), double_reaction_deletion on reactions[2:7], the capped 25-gene iJO1366 runs) are unnamed inline printed demonstrations with no stored result; the iJO1366 timing benchmark is a performance diagnostic; the PFK/pfkA/pfkB optimum prints are introductory diagnostics; knockout-indexer lookups are selections from already-exported tables. No full-computation endpoint exists in the source beyond the three exported. The double-deletion target set (diagonal included, 95+4465=4560) matches both the reference row count and the reference execution of double_target_set_complete (requiring exactly 95 bare diagonals plus all sorted unordered pairs), and the notebook's own double.knockout[{atpm}] singleton lookup corroborates the diagonal-inclusive semantics; the earlier pairs-only/96-reaction proposal description was correctly reconciled to the recorded 95-reaction model (137 genes / 95 reactions confirmed in the structural audit of the supplied input). The staged input is a byte-for-byte copy of the pinned cobra package's textbook.xml.gz, which is exactly what load_model('textbook') consumed, so input derivation is faithful with full lineage. No omitted endpoint, no scope change, and no additional source-side validation is required for this audit (native isolation, solver performance and release checks are later stages).
